soil-agri-061.q: What is the difference between shelterbelts and woodlots?
soil-agri-061.a: Shelterbelts are rows of trees set perpendicular to the prevailing wind, while woodlots are more extensive areas of woodland.

soil-agri-070.q: What is the smother effect of a flattened cover crop?
soil-agri-070.a: It forms a nearly impenetrable mat that blocks light, cutting weed germination.

soil-agri-079.q: What did the act passed after the Supreme Court struck down the Agricultural Adjustment Act do?
soil-agri-079.a: It amended and renamed the Soil Conservation Act of 1935 to preserve soil fertility and reduce exploitation and unprofitable use of national soil resources.

soil-agri-078.q: In what climate does this road dust suppressant work best, and what is its chief benefit?
soil-agri-078.a: It works better in humid than in arid climates, and its chief benefit is lower maintenance costs for gravel roads.

soil-agri-208.q: Why does keeping soil covered reduce erosion?
soil-agri-208.a: Water and wind erosion occur almost exclusively on exposed soil, and live plants protect it best.

soil-agri-206.q: When is erosion worst, and what does tillage do to runoff?
soil-agri-206.a: It is worst when soil has no living plants, roots or residue mulch; tillage that breaks aggregates lowers infiltration and worsens runoff.

soil-agri-213.q: How does more soil organic matter reduce runoff?
soil-agri-213.a: It gives better aggregation and less surface sealing, so more water infiltrates instead of running off and carrying soil away.

soil-agri-163.q: When is a remote sensor called active, and when passive?
soil-agri-163.a: It is active when it emits a signal and detects its reflection, and passive when it detects reflected sunlight.

soil-agri-166.q: Into which four categories of decreasing generality is this land suitability classification divided?
soil-agri-166.a: Orders (kinds of suitability), classes (degrees), subclasses (kinds of limitation) and units (minor management differences).

soil-agri-218.q: Why are large expanses of poor land mapped by reconnaissance survey?
soil-agri-218.a: They have little agricultural or forest value and are often too poor to justify a detailed survey, so they are mapped at small scale, showing soil associations.

soil-meth-023.q: How does atomic absorption measure a metal?
soil-meth-023.a: The metal is vaporized in a flame and absorbs at its own wavelengths; the absorbed radiation is proportional to the density of its atoms.

soil-meth-059.q: Which extractants suit acidic and alkaline soils in Washington and Oregon?
soil-meth-059.a: Bray 1 is used for acidic soils and Olsen for alkaline soils.

soil-meth-061.q: What can very high phosphorus in a soil test point to?
soil-meth-061.a: Years of heavy poultry or other manure.

soil-meth-027.q: What does the voltage of an ion-selective electrode depend on?
soil-meth-027.a: It depends on the logarithm of the ion's activity, following the Nernst equation, and is read against a reference electrode.

soil-meth-066.q: Why is human vision still needed in image analysis despite computers?
soil-meth-066.a: Computers are indispensable for large data and quantitative extraction, but human vision cannot be replaced in many applications.

soil-meth-045.q: Name two spatial autocorrelation statistics covered by spatial analysis.

soil-agri-090.q: What two factors does the scorpan model add to the classical five?
soil-agri-090.a: s, intrinsic soil properties captured by remote and proximal sensors, and n, spatial coordinates or position.

soil-meth-053.q: What does Cohen's kappa add to overall accuracy?
soil-meth-053.a: It corrects for chance agreement; both measures range from 0 to 1.

soil-meth-001.q: What was geostatistics first developed to predict?
soil-meth-001.a: The distribution of ore grades in mines.

soil-meth-004.q: What does regression kriging model separately?
soil-meth-004.a: The deterministic and stochastic parts of variation, following Matheron's 1969 universal model.

soil-meth-048.q: What must stratified sampling strata satisfy?
soil-meth-048.a: They must be collectively exhaustive and mutually exclusive, so every element falls in exactly one.

soil-meth-052.q: What does conditioned Latin hypercube sampling do?
soil-meth-052.a: It samples all covariates with one sample per stratum.

soil-meth-016.q: How does gamma-ray spectroscopy of soil identify elements?
soil-meth-016.a: Cosmic rays make nuclei emit gamma rays; each emission line's energy identifies an element and its intensity gives the concentration.

soil-meth-033.q: Who coined the term chemometrics, and when?
soil-meth-033.a: Svante Wold, in a 1971 grant application.

soil-env-106.q: How much carbon do soils hold compared with the atmosphere?
soil-env-106.a: About 2,700 Gt, roughly three times the carbon in the atmosphere.

soil-env-110.q: What does plant uptake do to carbon in soil?
soil-env-110.a: It fixes carbon dioxide in soil, building a pool of around 1500 Pg in the first few metres, 20-40% of it lasting more than 100 years.

soil-env-103.q: What does the fast carbon cycle include?
soil-env-103.a: It runs through living things, with annual cycles driven by photosynthesis and decadal cycles of vegetation growth and decomposition.

soil-env-105.q: Why does replacing forest with cropland leave more carbon in the atmosphere?
soil-env-105.a: Cropland and urban land store comparatively little carbon.

soil-env-141.q: What visible sign shows permafrost thaw weakening soil structure?
soil-env-141.a: Trees tilting at random, so-called drunken trees.

soil-env-147.q: What is active layer thickness, and what is its main control?
soil-env-147.a: It is the maximum thaw depth over two years; maximum air temperature is the main control.

soil-env-149.q: What does the Russian word behind this term mean?
soil-env-149.a: That which survives over the summer.

soil-env-127.q: What slows weathering as the soil solution saturates?
soil-env-127.a: Weathering slows as the soil solution saturates, so some argue low rainfall limits it.

soil-env-121.q: Why is glomalin's role in soil carbon thought overestimated?
soil-env-121.a: Most glomalin-extracted proteins proved not to be mycorrhizal, and arbuscular fungi were found to cause net soil carbon losses.

soil-env-058.q: How does degradation differ from retrogression?
soil-env-058.a: Degradation is directly tied to human activity, whereas retrogression is driven mainly by soil erosion.

soil-env-063.q: How much faster than soil forms does erosion from farm fields run?
soil-env-063.a: 11 to 20 times faster under no-tillage and more than 100 times faster under conventional tillage.

soil-env-059.q: Why does secondary succession run faster than primary succession?

soil-env-078.q: Why are Middle Eastern dust storms becoming more frequent and intense?
soil-env-078.a: Long-term rainfall decline lowers soil moisture and plant cover.

soil-env-069.q: How much of human-induced land degradation is due to unsustainable farming?
soil-env-069.a: Over 60%: it had degraded 996 Mha of agricultural land by 2025.

soil-env-321.q: Why do roots need pores wider than about 0.1 mm?
soil-env-321.a: It is the size of most root tips; without such pores roots stay short and thick with few fine roots or root hairs, poor at taking up water and nutrients.

soil-env-210.q: How do denser woody canopies affect soil moisture?
soil-env-210.a: They raise transpiration and evaporation of soil moisture, and enhanced soil porosity can speed soil drought.

soil-env-099.q: How can lightly degraded land be restored?
soil-env-099.a: It can be fenced from grazing, fertilized or weeded; grazing may continue at lower, monitored intensity, for example by rotating fields seasonally.

soil-env-308.q: How do deep roots help soil handle urban runoff?
soil-env-308.a: They open extra channels for infiltration, maintain soil permeability and sustain the microbes that break down pollutants and remove nitrogen.

soil-env-375.q: When is scraping the surface and replacing it with good topsoil feasible?
soil-env-375.a: When contamination is modest or shallow, since excavating contaminated soil is expensive and regulated.

soil-env-377.q: What two demands must a rooftop soil mix meet?
soil-env-377.a: It must be light enough not to overload the roof yet heavy enough to anchor plants against wind and water.

soil-env-195.q: What makes up a septic system?
soil-env-195.a: The drain field, septic tank and piping together, where a microbial ecosystem breaks down the organic materials in the liquid.

soil-agri-169.q: What remains the main disposal mechanism in conventional septic systems?
soil-agri-169.a: Decomposition by natural organisms, so minimum retention times and distances to surface water and wells are set.

soil-env-350.q: Why sample at least 10 spots when assessing soil health in the field?
soil-env-350.a: Measurements vary with moisture and season, so a single spot may mislead.

soil-env-365.q: Why do perennials give more carbon input than annuals?
soil-env-365.a: Because of larger root systems and a longer photosynthesis period.

soil-env-341.q: Why can routine soil fumigation or broad-spectrum herbicides backfire?
soil-env-341.a: They create dependency on purchased inputs, weaken resilience and promote resistance.

soil-env-193.q: How do industry and construction damage urban soil?
soil-env-193.a: Industry alters soil chemistry with heavy metals and effluents, while construction and landfills compact and excavate soil, disturbing water purification and storage.

soil-env-344.q: How do damaged plants call in help against caterpillars?
soil-env-344.a: They produce extra-floral nectar that feeds beneficials and airborne volatiles that guide small wasps to the caterpillar, in which the wasp lays eggs that kill it.

soil-env-360.q: Which soils suit no-till, and which suit strip-till or zone-till?
soil-env-360.a: Well-drained coarse soils suit no-till; finer-textured soils do well with strip-till or zone-till.

soil-env-327.q: Which soil properties change little, and which can management change?
soil-env-327.a: Inherent properties such as drainage and depth change little; management can change dynamic ones such as organic matter, structure, and water and nutrient holding capacity.

soil-env-367.q: How can compaction be avoided on larger farms?
soil-env-367.a: By monitoring axle loads and tire inflation and avoiding field work on wet soil.

soil-env-343.q: How does East African push-pull protect corn?
soil-env-343.a: Desmodium within corn rows repels stem borers (push) and perimeter grasses attract adult moths (pull).

soil-env-346.q: Why does optimal soil health underpin pest management?
soil-env-346.a: Healthy, thriving plants defend themselves better, while stressed plants signal weakness to pests.

soil-env-009.q: Why can wiping out part of the base of the food chain matter?
soil-env-009.a: It can have major consequences for predators and other consumers.

soil-env-005.q: When did use of this pesticide peak, and why did it fall?
soil-env-005.a: Use peaked at 72,000 tonnes in 1970 and then fell as its harm became clear.

soil-env-249.q: What governs action on contaminated land where no standards exist?

soil-env-008.q: Which metals and compounds are linked to cancer or birth defects after long exposure?
soil-env-008.a: Chromium, lead and other metals, petroleum, solvents and many pesticides.

soil-env-242.q: What does a groundwater pollutant often form, and where can it reach?
soil-env-242.a: A plume that spreads through the aquifer and can reach wells, seeps and springs.

soil-env-032.q: Why do bioaugmentation attempts often fail?
soil-env-032.a: Failures come from the wrong organism, predation, competition with native bacteria and too-small doses.

soil-env-049.q: What do the seven letters-factors of the DRASTIC index describe, and what does a lower index mean?
soil-env-049.a: They cover depth to water, net recharge, aquifer media, soil media, topography, vadose zone impact and hydraulic conductivity; a lower index means lower risk of aquifer contamination.

soil-env-314.a: Sewage sludges treated to lower pathogen risk, widely used as soil amendments.

soil-env-043.q: How does rhizofiltration differ from phytoextraction?
soil-env-043.a: It traps contaminants, mainly heavy metals, in harvestable biomass but treats water, while phytoextraction treats soil.

soil-env-232.q: What is bioavailability, and why does it matter for biodegradation?
soil-env-232.a: It is the amount of a pollutant physically accessible to microbes, and it is a key factor in efficient biodegradation.

soil-env-317.q: Why does removing fines reduce the soil to treat?
soil-env-317.a: Contaminants cling to the fines, so removing them reduces total mass and volume.

soil-env-288.q: In which groups is eating soil documented?
soil-env-288.a: In over 100 primate species and, in humans, most often in children and pregnant women, classed as a form of pica.

soil-env-295.q: Where is iodine deficiency common, and what does it cause?
soil-env-295.a: In remote inland and mountainous areas with iodine-poor soil and no marine foods; it causes goitre and developmental delay.

soil-env-305.q: How are prions transmitted to grazing animals through soil?
soil-env-305.a: By eating grass growing in contaminated soil; they stay infectious for years and bind tightly to soil particles.

soil-hist-147.q: What does photosynthesis usually mean, and what does it release?
soil-hist-147.a: Oxygenic photosynthesis, which splits water and releases oxygen.

soil-hist-124.q: What builds up trapped charge in buried quartz or feldspar grains?
soil-hist-124.a: Natural radiation from cosmic rays and traces of potassium, uranium, thorium and rubidium.

soil-hist-149.q: Why is glycolate a problem for photosynthesis?
soil-hist-149.a: It is toxic at high concentration and inhibits photosynthesis.

soil-hist-125.q: Why must luminescence grains be extracted without exposure to light?
soil-hist-125.a: Light frees the trapped electrons, so exposure would release the signal.

soil-hist-122.q: Which fraction of peat gives the most reliable radiocarbon date?
soil-hist-122.a: The humins, because they are insoluble in alkali and less contaminated.

soil-hist-130.q: Where does excess lead-210 in surface soils come from?
soil-hist-130.a: Atmospheric fallout of radon-222 decay products.

soil-hist-036.q: What did Josiah Wedgwood suggest caused the buried lime and cinders at Maer Hall?

soil-hist-143.q: Where did this soil salinity research begin?
soil-hist-143.a: At Hisar in 1969, moving to Karnal that year.

soil-hist-032.q: What did soil surveys mainly serve before 1950?

soil-hist-106.q: What did this man experiment with in his twenties, and why?
soil-hist-106.a: Marl, to rejuvenate land worn out by more than a century of tobacco monoculture.

soil-hist-110.q: What did he show about where plants get their carbon?
soil-hist-110.a: Plants take their carbon from atmospheric carbon dioxide, not from soil humus.

soil-hist-017.q: Who invented the enrichment culture, and why was it hard to isolate nitrifiers?
soil-hist-017.a: Martinus Beijerinck invented it; early nitrification researchers could at first only enrich cultures of nitrifiers rather than isolate them pure.

soil-hist-047.q: What is the purpose of this international soil science union?
soil-hist-047.a: To promote all branches of soil science and their applications, foster contacts among soil scientists, and stimulate research and its use.

soil-hist-052.q: When did Milton Whitney begin field work?

soil-hist-056.q: What was the main contribution of this NRCS committee?
soil-hist-056.a: Improving technical standards for describing anthropogenic soils and defining the taxa to classify them.
